20A.8 New priests are to be anointed, consecrated and sanctified.

precepts.text: At the consecration Moses put the ephod and breastplate on Aaron, and he put in the breastplate the Urim and the Thummim.
precepts.point: Joshua likewise was to stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask counsel for him after the judgment of Urim before the Lord; the Most High gave revelation through it.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
At the consecration Moses did what Exodus 28 commanded. He “washed them with water”, put the coat, the girdle and the robe on Aaron, “put the ephod upon him, and he girded him with the curious girdle of the ephod, and bound it unto him therewith. And he put the breastplate upon him: also he put in the breastplate the Urim and the Thummim.”

So the Urim and the Thummim went into the breastplate of judgment, upon Aaron's heart before the Lord, exactly as commanded. Urim and Thummim means lights and perfections: objects not specifically described in the scriptures, perhaps stones since they went in the breastplate, by which the high priest ascertained the will of the Most High in important matters affecting the nation. To ascertain is to find out for certain, a divine discerning beyond what a man can determine by his own thinking.

precepts.text: Unity among brethren is like the precious ointment upon Aaron's head that ran down his beard to the skirts of his garments; for there the LORD commanded the blessing.
precepts.point: This is what David is going back to in the psalm: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; it is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard, down to the skirts of his garments. That oil could be poured on no one but the high priest; that is how precious unity among the people is to be.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
Moses poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head and anointed him, to sanctify him, to set him apart. That is what David is going back to: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity! It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron’s beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments”.

That oil could be poured on no one but the high priest; that is how precious unity among the people is to be. It is like the dew too: “As the dew of Hermon, and as the dew that descended upon the mountains of Zion: for there the Lord commanded the blessing, even life for evermore.”

precepts.text: The sin offering and the burnt offering were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel; the purified altar carried that reconciliation.
precepts.point: The fat, the caul, and the kidneys, the guts, were burnt upon the altar, but the bullock with his hide and flesh was burnt with fire without the camp. Christ's crucifixion lines up with the law of sacrifice: he was taken outside Jerusalem to the place called Golgotha and crucified there.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
Moses put the blood upon the horns of the altar, purified the altar, and sanctified it, to make reconciliation upon it. Reconciliation goes back to what the prince prepares: “the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.”

The purified altar carried that reconciliation for the house of Israel. And the bullock with his hide and flesh burnt with fire without the camp lines up with Christ’s crucifixion: he was taken outside Jerusalem to the place called Golgotha and crucified there.

precepts.text: They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; the sprinkled blood of the law is the shadow of that blood.
precepts.point: The blood, sprinkled again and again about the altar, is spiritual: they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony, which is the Bible, and they loved not their lives unto the death. That is how Satan and all the nations are overcome; the blood of the sacrifices went all the way back to Christ.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
The blood, sprinkled again and again about the altar and upon Aaron and his sons and their garments, is spiritual: “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.”

The word of their testimony is the Bible. That is how Satan and all the nations are overcome: by the blood of the Lamb and the word. The sprinkled blood of the law is the shadow of that blood; the blood of the sacrifices went all the way back to Christ.

points: Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and a bullock for the sin offering, and two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread; and all the congregation was gathered unto the door of the tabernacle.

Mark the list: if you want to live under the Old Covenant, you had better have a priest, the garments, the anointing oil, a bullock for the sin offering, two rams, a basket of unleavened bread, and a temple to gather at. The covenant of sacrifice cannot be kept today.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses washed Aaron and his sons with water, and put upon him the coat, the girdle, the robe, and the ephod, and he put the breastplate upon him, and in the breastplate the Urim and the Thummim.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: He put the mitre upon his head, and upon the mitre, upon his forefront, the golden plate, the holy crown, as the LORD commanded Moses.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses anointed the tabernacle and all that was therein, sprinkled the altar seven times, and poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron's head, and anointed him, to sanctify him, to set him apart.

This is what David is going back to in the psalm: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; it is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard, down to the skirts of his garments. That oil could be poured on no one but the high priest; that is how precious unity among the people is to be.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the bullock for the sin offering, and Moses put the blood upon the horns of the altar with his finger, purified the altar, and sanctified it, to make reconciliation upon it; reconciliation goes back to making reconciliation for the house of Israel.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The fat, the caul, and the kidneys, the guts, were burnt upon the altar, but the bullock with his hide and flesh was burnt with fire without the camp. Christ's crucifixion lines up with the law of sacrifice: he was taken outside Jerusalem to the place called Golgotha and crucified there.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The ram for the burnt offering was cut into pieces, the inwards and legs washed in water, and Moses burnt the whole ram upon the altar: a burnt sacrifice for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses slew the other ram, the ram of consecration, and put the blood upon the tip of Aaron's right ear, upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, and the same for his sons.

The blood went on the right side. The right side is the favored side with the Most High, and the volume of the book bears the pattern: when Christ rose he went to his Father and sat on the right hand of God.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The fat, the right shoulder, and out of the basket one unleavened cake, a cake of oiled bread, and one wafer were put upon the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved for a wave offering before the LORD, then burnt on the altar for a sweet savour.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses took the breast and waved it for a wave offering before the LORD, lifting it up and waving it as in Exodus 29; it was Moses' part of the ram of consecration.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses sprinkled the anointing oil and the blood upon Aaron and his garments and upon his sons and their garments, and sanctified them. They boiled the flesh at the door of the tabernacle and ate it there with the bread of consecration, and abode at the door of the tabernacle day and night seven days, until the days of their consecration were at an end.

The blood, sprinkled again and again about the altar, is spiritual: they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony, which is the Bible, and they loved not their lives unto the death. That is how Satan and all the nations are overcome; the blood of the sacrifices went all the way back to Christ.
